items.claim: The unit's load-bearing structural warrant — an infinitive purpose chain running unbroken to the unit's own close — is not what the pointed bytes carry, and the finite-clause differentia used to place the seam at Isa.61.4 is already met one clause earlier, inside this span.
items.evidence: Seven lamed-prefixed infinitives do run from Isa.61.1 to the middle of Isa.61.3 — לְבַשֵּׂ֣ר, לַחֲבֹ֣שׁ, לִקְרֹ֤א (oshb:Isa.61.1), לִקְרֹ֤א, לְנַחֵ֖ם (oshb:Isa.61.2), לָשׂ֣וּם, לָתֵת֩ (oshb:Isa.61.3), all byte tier — but two finite perfects sit inside that stretch and break it twice before Isa.61.2: מָשַׁח֩ and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier), the second of them the very sending the chain is said to be governed by, and the English witness renders both finite as well. The clause quoted as the unit's close is itself finite-headed: וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) is waw-plus-perfect, the identical construction to וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) that is offered as the differentia at the seam — so the stated criterion is satisfied at Isa.61.3's second half, inside the span, and the closing לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר is governed by that finite clause rather than by the sending. The disclosed catchword needs re-tiering too: only לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר is byte-identical across the pair, and it stands in exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, oshb:Isa.60.21 and oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier); the planting-noun side is skeleton grade (sweep: 3 verses on that consonantal string, oshb:Isa.14.19, oshb:Isa.60.21, oshb:Isa.61.3) and the oshb:Isa.60.21 token is a ketiv/qere pair — מטעו unpointed against מַטָּעַ֛י pointed — quoted in neither form and disclosed as neither, so a claim about a 'collocation' there rests on an apparatus-doubled reading. Against oshb:Isa.61.3's מַטַּ֥ע the link is one consonantal skeleton, not a repeated form. What holds: the servant-referent hold is byte-true — no eved-root token stands in oshb:Isa.61.1-Isa.61.3 (sweep: 46 verses book-wide, none in chs 61-62) — and אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Isa.61.1) re-collates at byte tier, as does the setumah at oshb:Isa.60.22 in the inventory.

items.claim: The internal-texture reading and the close at Isa.61.9 hold on the bytes: no tier-1 frame formula stands anywhere in this stretch of the book, and the closing referent shift is byte-true.
items.evidence: All three quoted runs re-collate at byte tier against their cited verses — וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4), וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.6), כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8). The claim that the Isa.61.6 and Isa.61.8 shifts carry no frame of their own is byte-confirmed rather than merely asserted: the messenger formula, the postpositive oracle signature, the woe cry and the burden header are each absent from chs 60-64 (sweep: 0 verses in that stretch for each of the four objects), and no vocative marker stands at either shift, so they are pronoun texture. The setumah at oshb:Isa.61.9 is inventory-correct, correctly typed, correctly labelled single-witness, and it is the only span-relevant seg (1 seg over Isa.61.4-Isa.61.9) — the disclosure is complete. Two residuals are recorded here rather than treated as defeaters, since neither touches the evidence the unit actually rests on. First, the front seam shares its construction with the clause before it: וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3) is the same waw-plus-perfect as וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4), both byte tier, and לָהֶם֙ at Isa.61.3 is resumed as the unstated plural subject of Isa.61.4. Second, two lexical hooks reach across the back seam: פְּאֵ֜ר (oshb:Isa.61.3) against פְּאֵ֔ר (oshb:Isa.61.10) is accent_stripped-identical with differing accents, and that standalone token stands in exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses); the priest root recurs as כֹּהֲנֵ֤י (oshb:Isa.61.6) against יְכַהֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.61.10), the same consonants under medial/final nun allography (sweep: 4 verses for each attested spelling, the two spellings being separate sweep objects). Both belong to the neighbouring unit's front seam, not to this unit's own argument.

items.claim: Two undisclosed lexical hooks in this unit's own opening verse reach back across its front seam into both preceding units, and its close rests on the chapter division plus a genre contrast rather than on anything the bytes mark.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.61.10 reaches back twice. פְּאֵ֜ר (oshb:Isa.61.3) and פְּאֵ֔ר (oshb:Isa.61.10) are accent_stripped-identical, differing only in accent, and that standalone token stands in exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses) — the garland given in the earlier unit is the garland worn in this one. The priest root recurs as כֹּהֲנֵ֤י (oshb:Isa.61.6) against יְכַהֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.61.10), the same consonants under medial/final nun allography (sweep: 4 verses for each attested spelling). Under the standing cross-seam rule a byte-true device straddling a unit's own seam argues continuity against it unless disclosed; neither is disclosed here, while the unit opening at Isa.61.1 did disclose the structurally identical hook at its own edge — the disclosure is asymmetric within one chapter. At the back seam the stated warrant is the chapter division, which is tier-4 metadata and never boundary evidence, plus a content contrast between a rejoicing report and a vow. The bytes supply nothing in its place: the first-person-singular voice is continuous — שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ (oshb:Isa.61.10) against אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1), all byte tier — and no frame formula intervenes (sweep: 0 verses carrying the messenger formula, the oracle signature, the woe cry or the burden header in chs 60-64). The parashah inventory records no seg at oshb:Isa.61.11; that is disclosure, not counterevidence. The setumah cited at oshb:Isa.61.9 is inventory-correct and correctly typed, and both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier.

items.claim: The seam is carried by an 'explicit vocative' and a 'new first-person divine act' at Isa.62.6 that the bytes do not supply, while the second-feminine-singular addressee runs straight through it, suffixed tokens standing in six of the seven verses Isa.62.2-Isa.62.8.
items.evidence: At oshb:Isa.62.6 the city name יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם stands unmarked between חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ and הִפְקַ֨דְתִּי֙ (byte tier); there is no vocative particle or marker in the bytes, so 'explicit vocative' reads the English witness's comma back into the Hebrew — a form-class claim the staged evidence cannot settle, and one that should be held rather than made the seam's driver. The second-feminine-singular addressee is continuous across the claimed seam: accent-stripped 2fs-suffixed tokens run oshb:Isa.62.2 (3 tokens), oshb:Isa.62.3 (1), oshb:Isa.62.4 (6), oshb:Isa.62.5 (4), oshb:Isa.62.6 (1), oshb:Isa.62.8 (3), oshb:Isa.62.7 alone carrying none — this unit's own last two words are עָלַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5) and the next verse's first suffixed word is חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ, the same addressee either side, and דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ, לְאֹ֣יְבַ֔יִךְ, תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.8) carry it on past the next seam. 'New first-person divine act' fails on both qualifiers: oshb:Isa.62.1 already carries two first-person-singular verbs, אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (byte tier), so the person is not new, and neither speaker is named anywhere in Isa.62.1-Isa.62.6 — the divine attribution at Isa.62.6 is inference, exactly the kind of unnamed-speaker identification a chunking decision should leave open. The recorded confidence sits at the top of the scale and the bytes do not carry it. Credit where due: the ketiv/qere handling at oshb:Isa.62.3 is exemplary — וצנוף וּצְנִ֥יף quotes both staged forms side by side, unpointed ketiv against pointed qere, re-collating at byte tier, and the inventory does record one note at that verse; and the mark-absence statement for oshb:Isa.61.11 and Isa.62.1-Isa.62.5 is inventory-correct and is not leaned on as counterevidence.

items.claim: The cohesion argument and the rejected alternative both attribute the 'give no rest' summons to the watchmen, but in the bytes that summons is addressed to them by the same speaker who posted them.
items.evidence: The second half of oshb:Isa.62.6 and all of oshb:Isa.62.7 are second-person-plural and directed outward: הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier) — לָכֶֽם is an addressed form and תִּתְּנ֥וּ is an addressed form, and the English witness reads the same way. No petition is uttered by the watchmen anywhere in Isa.62.6-Isa.62.9; the commands are laid on them. So 'the watchmen's own summons' and 'the watchmen's own petition' name a speech role the bytes do not attest, and the unifying claim that the oath answers that petition loses its ground — which also empties the rejected alternative, since the reason given for not splitting at Isa.62.8 is that the sworn content answers a petition that is not there. A second consequence the bytes force: the addressee alternates inside this span — 2fs at חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.6), 2mp at לָכֶֽם and תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.6-Isa.62.7), 2fs again at דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ and תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.8) — and that alternation is undisclosed even though an addressee shift is precisely what this unit's own front-seam argument turns on; the front seam inherits the further problem that the 2fs addressee runs from oshb:Isa.62.2 to oshb:Isa.62.8, suffixed tokens in six of those seven verses. What holds: נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.62.8) re-collates at byte tier and does introduce the oath-negative construction that runs to the unit's close, and the setumah at oshb:Isa.62.9 is inventory-correct, correctly typed and the only span-relevant seg.

items.claim: Both edges are genuinely corroborated, but the stated onset differentia does not discriminate: the group commanded at Isa.62.10 is the same unnamed second-person-plural group already commanded in the preceding verses.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.62.10 does open with a dense positive imperative run — עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ … פַּנּ֖וּ … סֹ֣לּוּ סֹ֤לּוּ … סַקְּל֣וּ … הָרִ֥ימוּ (byte tier), seven addressed-plural imperative tokens including two doubled pairs — but the immediately preceding verses already command an unnamed addressed-plural group: אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6) and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7), byte tier. 'Addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing' the preceding address therefore states a continuity as though it were a break, and the contrast is drawn against a 'watchmen's own petition' that the bytes do not attest, since those commands are laid on the addressees rather than spoken by them. The bracketing claim is under-specified in the same direction: what answers וְקָרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם … וְלָךְ֙ יִקָּרֵ֣א (oshb:Isa.62.12, byte tier) is וְקֹ֤רָא לָךְ֙ שֵׁ֣ם חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) and the renaming at oshb:Isa.62.4, neither quoted nor cited, not the resolve at Isa.62.1. The 2fs addressee also runs into this span — יִשְׁעֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.11) and the second-person form in וְלָךְ֙ יִקָּרֵ֣א (oshb:Isa.62.12), 1 suffixed token each, continuous with oshb:Isa.62.8. Severity is held low because the seam itself is the best-corroborated in this stretch and the disclosure is complete: setumah segs stand at oshb:Isa.62.9 and oshb:Isa.62.12, both inventory-correct, both correctly typed, both labelled single-witness, both disclosed for the two edges they touch, and both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier.

items.claim: The dialogue frame is real but its byte architecture is misdescribed: the doubled opening question exists only in the English rendering, the unit's genuine second question at Isa.63.2 is neither quoted nor cited, and the Masoretic apparatus claims are keyed to the wrong numbering space.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.63.1 has 18 tokens and carries the interrogative exactly once — מִי זֶ֣ה בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם (byte tier). The second clause opens זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ (byte tier): a bare demonstrative, no interrogative at all (the demonstrative occurs twice in the verse, the interrogative once). The English witness supplies 'Who is this' a second time, so a frame described as the voice twice opening with the same challenge inside one verse is translation-dependent and does not survive into the Hebrew; that interrogative-plus-demonstrative opener is a one-off in the book (sweep: 1 verse). 'Vocative challenge' is also the wrong class — the opener is interrogative, not vocative. The real second question is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.63.2, מַדּ֥וּעַ אָדֹ֖ם לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ (byte tier; sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry that interrogative, oshb:Isa.5.4, oshb:Isa.50.2, oshb:Isa.63.2), which makes the byte-level shape question / answer / question / answer across Isa.63.1-Isa.63.6 rather than a doubled opener answered once. That verse appears in neither the prose nor the evidence refs, so the strongest byte support for the very frame being argued goes unused, and the rejected alternative's own reasoning — that no sub-seam signal stands inside the exchange — is argued without the one verse that most bears on it. Second defect: the Masoretic apparatus is cited under the English witness's coordinates. The two setumah segs and the two paseq segs are keyed web:, while both inventories are Masoretic-keyed, and the other units in this stretch key the same claims oshb:. Chs 62-63 are identity numbering, so the arithmetic is harmless here, but this span sits in the chapter whose closing verse is the book's split verse, where one Masoretic verse spans two verses in the English witness and the numbering space is decisive; a witness-mislabelled apparatus claim three verses either side of that would be a live error. The apparatus content is right and deserves credit: setumah at oshb:Isa.62.12 and oshb:Isa.63.6, one paseq seg each at oshb:Isa.63.1 and oshb:Isa.63.3, no intra-verse position asserted, single-witness labelled, and the quoted Hebrew re-collates at byte tier.
